description.narrative:
Over the past ten years UNEP, via the SUN facility, has worked on internalizing environmental sustainability management across the UN system. The SUN facility 2018-2021 project is just concluding, and it is marked a strong shift in the UNâ€™s sustainability efforts. At the demand of the Secretary General the HLCM and UNEP (via the EMG) were tasked to raise their ambitions to reduce the UN's environmental footprint and to demonstrate leadership by practicing what it preaches. This call resulted in the 2019 adoption of the Strategy for Sustainability Strategy I in May 2019.
For the new SUN facility project, the situation, in many respects, is very different from the previous projects. UNEP, via the SUN project and the EMG, must adapt to vastly increased needs and expectations from both the UN Executive Office and from Member States. This leads to a change in focus of the project and its objectives to better: 1) align with the UN Sustainability Strategy, 2) support the integration of environmental objectives in the UN reforms, and 3) assist UN organizations in integrating, not just five (5) but 37 environmental objectives into their management and operations. The project must also develop a reporting system that allows entities to transparently highlight results and challenges to Member States, Senior Management, and the Executive Office.
The shift also provides for a better connection to the integration of the UN reforms and the UN in system actions and policies aimed to mitigate the triple-challenge of the climate, biodiversity, and pollution crises including. These aspects require that SUN broaden its scope and reach and that the project integrates additional elements able to support the increased expectations from the UN system and Member States with regards to â€œGreening the Blueâ€.
An additional fact which necessitates a shift in focus for SUN is that the present rate of realized impact reductions is insufficient to fully meet existing commitments. This short-coming is linked to four interlocking factors: 1) A misalignment between publicly declared Member State expectations of the UN's own environmental performance and the means and political pressure exerted on UN top managers. 2)The inconsistent attention and prioritization of environmental performance by Member States also influences the management culture of UN entities, failing to discourage a culture that prioritizes the short-term cost reductions instead of reviewing life cycle and total cost of ownership for such decisions. 3) the UN Sustainability Strategy, which the CEB expects UNEP to support, as well as the QCPR Decision have a wide reach and set of objectives which demand a corresponding resource mobilization effort and the technical assistance necessary to support the UN in its new ambitions cannot be reached by the SUN team in its current configuration. 4) Lastly, the challenge related to knowledge management and outreach. The current increase in attention from Member States, UN top management and other international organizations is not matched with sufficient efforts in communication nor by a comprehensive and accessible package of policies and tools. Additionally, there remain many UN staff who are unaware, or unmotivated, by the urgency of action which is required or of the availability of numerous tools and approaches which can further enable meeting their environmental targets.
Therefore, the SUN project aims to broaden the scope, scale, and rate of environmental impact reductions from UN entities via four main Outputs, as identified above, 1) Knowledge and policy co-creation, management, and networking; 2) Communication, reporting, and advocacy; 3) Data analytics, indicators, and 2050 Readiness; and 4) Greening through UN Reforms. These four areas are each directly linked to key pathways for change, providing for activities and outputs in line with the identified outcome as well as reflective of the principal drivers for unlocking action and implementing the needed reductions to the UN systems environmental impacts. Ultimately, these four outputs result in the Project Outcome: "All UN entities are reporting, mainstreaming, and implementing the environmental dimensions of the Global 2030 Agenda for their management functions in line with targets and indicators identified in the Sustainability Strategy Phase I via Greening the Blue."
